verdict.rationale: A filing agency could fairly publish third-party authorization rules, so this axis applies. The evidence only mentions a list of registered agents, that a Delaware-located business may act as its own agent, and that agents serve as a de facto service layer. It never documents authorization forms, the scope of a third party's permitted actions, or which signatures must stay personal, so registered agents are an adjacent feature, not the delegated-access disclosure the story asks for.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal
